title: CTAB Extraction of DNA and RNA from Respiratory Samples
author: Leah Cuthbertson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf28jqhw

steps.title: Prepare phenol:chloroform:isoamyl stock
steps.instruction: In a fume cupboard, add the required volume of working stock Phenol:Chloroform:Isoamyl (P:C:I, ratio 25:24:1) to a 50 mL Falcon tube; use a 10 mL pipette to withdraw the volume from below the top buffered layer of the stock bottle. For a new bottle, first add the buffer and allow it to settle before use.

steps.title: Prepare chloroform:isoamyl stock
steps.instruction: In the same fume cupboard, add the required volume of working stock Chloroform:Isoamyl (C:I, ratio 24:1) to a 50 mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Add linear polyacrylamide to eppendorfs
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL linear polyacrylamide (LPA) to each 2 mL Eppendorf tube; use two tubes per sample. LPA acts as a carrier and co‑precipitates with nucleic acids without affecting downstream use.

steps.title: Pre‑spin phase‑lock gel tubes
steps.instruction: Place one 2 mL Phase‑Lock Gel tube (Hard gel, catalog #733‑2478) per sample in a centrifuge and spin at 16 000 × g for 5 min. Ensure the gel is pelleted at the bottom (often on the sides).

steps.title: Add aluminium ammonium sulfate to LME tubes
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL aluminium ammonium sulfate to each Lysing Matrix E (LME) tube. Write the sample number on the lid and on the side of the tube (numbers may be rubbed off by the bead‑beater).

steps.title: Transfer sample and add CTAB, incubate
steps.instruction: Aseptically transfer the specimen into the LME tube, add 500 µL CTAB extraction buffer, and incubate at room temperature for 15 min (00:15:00).

substeps.instruction: Bacterial isolates: grow overnight, spin 2 mL broth 10 min at 16 000 × g, add 500 µL CTAB, resuspend pellet, incubate 15 min; bacteria/CTAB may be frozen before extraction; no extra CTAB needed.
Upper‑respiratory swabs: place a sterile spin basket in a 1.5 mL tube, keep swab on ice, cut tip with autoclaved scissors, transfer tip into LME tube, add 500 µL CTAB, incubate 15 min.
Upper‑respiratory lavage/aspirates: spin at full speed 20 min (minimum 2 mL, optimal 5 mL), resuspend pellet in 500 µL CTAB, transfer to LME tube.
Saliva or mouth‑wash: transfer ≤300 µL into LME tube.
Sputum (spontaneous or induced): transfer ≤300 µg or one sputum plug into LME tube.
Synthetic absorptive matrix (SAM) strips: cut with autoclaved scissors, keep on ice, transfer strip into LME tube.
Lung brushes: keep on ice, transfer to LME tube.
Bronchoalveolar lavage or pleural fluid: spin 20 min (minimum 2 mL, optimal 5 mL), resuspend pellet in 500 µL CTAB, transfer to LME tube (no further CTAB required).
Lung tissue (human or mouse) and lung biopsies: keep on ice, transfer to LME tube.
CSF: standardise volume, spin 20 min at 16 000 × g, resuspend pellet in 500 µL CTAB, transfer to LME tube (no further CTAB required).
All patient‑sample transfers must be performed in a Class 2 safety hood.

steps.title: Add phenol:chloroform:isoamyl to LME tubes
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, immediately add 500 µL P:C:I (25:24:1) to each LME tube. Pre‑wet the pipette tip to avoid drips caused by vapour pressure. Wear double gloves; if a small spill occurs, discard the outer gloves. Do not leave tubes with P:C:I for extended periods as it can degrade plastic.

steps.title: Bead‑beat samples (CTAB program)
steps.instruction: Transfer the LME tubes to the bead‑beater and run the pre‑programmed CTAB setting for 60 seconds (00:01:00): Speed 5.5 m / s, Adapter Quickprep, Lysing Matrix E, 1 mL quantity, 1 cycle, 300 s pause. Return tubes to ice immediately after beating. Ensure lids are tightly sealed, no beads are in the seal, and tubes are labelled on top and side.

steps.title: Centrifuge LME tubes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bead‑beaten LME tubes at 16 000 × g for 5 min (00:05:00).

steps.title: Transfer lysate to phase‑lock gel tube
steps.instruction: Transfer all liquid from each LME tube to a pre‑spun Phase‑Lock Gel tube; keep the original LME tube on ice. Centrifuge the Phase‑Lock Gel tube at 16 000 × g for 5 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge phase‑lock tube at 4 °C
steps.instruction: Place the Phase‑Lock Gel tube in a refrigerated centrifuge and spin at 16 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. A gel barrier will form separating the aqueous phase from the P:C:I/C:I phases.

steps.title: Add chloroform:isoamyl, mix, centrifuge
steps.instruction: Add one volume of C:I (24:1) to each Phase‑Lock Gel tube, shake briefly to mix, then centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C. If the barrier does not form, extend the centrifugation time.

steps.title: Second extraction: add reagents to bead‑beating tube
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add to each bead‑beating tube: 50 µL aluminium ammonium sulfate, 500 µL CTAB extraction buffer, and 500 µL P:C:I (25:24:1).

steps.title: Repeat bead‑beat and phase‑lock steps
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 8 through 12 (bead‑beating, centrifugation, transfer to Phase‑Lock Gel, refrigerated centrifugation, addition of C:I and centrifugation) using the reagents added in the second extraction.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase to eppendorfs with LPA
steps.instruction: Carefully pour the aqueous phase from each Phase‑Lock Gel tube into pre‑prepared Eppendorf tubes that already contain 1 µL LPA. Use up to two Eppendorf tubes per sample if needed to accommodate the volume for subsequent PEG addition.

steps.title: Add PEG/NaCl and precipitate overnight
steps.instruction: Add two volumes of PEG/NaCl solution to each tube, mix thoroughly (solution is viscous), and incubate at 4 °C overnight to precipitate nucleic acids. If time‑pressed, incubate for 2 h (yield will be reduced).

steps.title: Centrifuge PEG precipitate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge all Eppendorf tubes at 16 000 × g for 20 min (00:20:00) at 4 °C.

steps.title: Aspirate supernatant and ethanol washes
steps.instruction: Carefully aspirate the PEG/NaCl supernatant from each pellet (pellets are large, translucent, and uniform). Wash the pellet with 500 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge at 16 000 × g for 5 min. Repeat the ethanol wash twice more using 200 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol each time, centrifuging 5 min after each wash.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet and resuspend in TE
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for ~5 min, then resuspend in 30 µL low‑EDTA TE buffer. Combine the resuspended nucleic acid from each sample into a single tube (total 60 µL per sample). For sputum or other high‑biomass samples, increase to 50 µL per tube (100 µL total). Recommended storage tubes: tethered O‑ring sterile tubes (StarLab catalog #E1405‑2142, 0.5 mL plain skirted tube).

steps.title: Store nucleic acid extract
steps.instruction: Store the final nucleic‑acid extract at –20 °C or –80 °C until required.
